pre_registration.derived_margin_rule1_note: The ONE numeric bound the lane commits to is DERIVED, not chosen (see pre_data_amendment_20260920 for the pre-data correction): the open-loop cross-build velocity margin. v_{t+1} = v_t (1 - dt*d_eff) + dt*a with d_eff in [damping*0.95, damping] (the declared warm-start coupling) and a in [0, a_max = 0.55*1.8 = 0.99]. Envelope: |v_t| <= V = a_max/d_lo = 2.977443609022557 m/s (contraction fixed point, d_lo = damping*0.95). Build N+1 scales every d_eff by (1+delta), delta = 0.01: Delta_{t+1} = (1-dt*d'_t)Delta_t - dt*delta*d_t*v_t, hence max|Delta_v| <= delta*V/(1.01*0.95) = 0.03103119967715015 m/s at EVERY horizon. The margin applies to OPEN-LOOP registered cases (identical pinned command stream into both builds -- the only configuration where same-input-only-physics-changed is true). Closed-loop cross-build runs are recorded as evidence with the envelope gate only (|v_t| <= V for all t); no closeness claim is made on them.

rule_0.statement: THE COMPATIBILITY-CERTIFICATE GATE (Astra round 5). THE THEORY: a deployment gate built on a hash-bound 5-tuple certificate carrying (a) execution identity, (b) a complete restart-state inventory, (c) hash-chained replay evidence, (d) declared qualification scope, makes ANY silent incompatible deployment STRUCTURALLY DETECTABLE: every state that could change future behavior is either hash-bound in the certificate or the resumed/requalified trajectory moves measurably; and the gate has NO false positives on the unmodified artifacts (clean runs are byte-identical). A description ('we tested compatibility') survives any result; THIS gate can lose -- the falsifiers below name the exact injections that would kill it, and each is run for real in this lane.

prediction.P1_silent_promotion_caught_F1: The two F1 injections are CAUGHT: (i) perturbing ONE periodic state hash inside the certificate's evidence chain makes validate() return a chain-mismatch violation and the deploy check BLOCK; (ii) swapping ONE normalization constant in a COPIED manifest moves the canonical manifest hash (the P3 clause-b property), so the deployment request's compat_key no longer matches the certificate's and the deploy check BLOCKS; the tampered manifest also moves the corpus action bytes (second detection). FALSIFIER: either injection validates/passes the deploy check (deploys UNDETECTED).
prediction.P2_resume_drift_detected_F2: A checkpoint restart that would change the future trajectory is DETECTED TWICE: dropping the RNG stream (or the warm-start cache) from a restart snapshot makes (i) the snapshot loader REFUSE structurally, naming the missing inventory item, and (ii) the FORCED resume (bypassing the loader) produce a continuation TRAJECTORY that differs from the uninterrupted reference -- measured on the declared F2 instrument (pre_data_amendment_2): the tick-wise state-hash sequence and/or the applied-action byte stream (the RNG drop moves the state hashes from the first tick; the warm-start drop moves both, the damping coupling is observed). ONLY the complete snapshot resumes silently, and its continuation is BIT-IDENTICAL to the uninterrupted run in BOTH instruments. FALSIFIER: an incomplete snapshot loads without a named refusal, OR a forced trajectory-changing omission resumes identical on BOTH instruments, OR the COMPLETE snapshot resume differs by one byte or one state hash from uninterrupted.
prediction.P3_legacy_action_drift_detected_F3: On the frozen observation/command corpus (built NOW through P3's frozen loader over the pinned 900-tick slice, action bytes sha-pinned at corpus build, runtime pinned in the certificate), altering ONE action-mapping entry in a copied manifest (action scale[2] 0.4 -> 0.400001) changes the recomputed corpus action bytes; the byte comparison DETECTS the drift, and the manifest hash moves as the structural second detection. FALSIFIER: the altered mapping reproduces the pinned corpus bytes byte-identically in the same runtime.
prediction.P4_no_false_positives: THREE clean full-gate runs on the unmodified artifacts (scene run -> certificate issue -> validate -> deploy check ALLOW -> checks 1-3 -> corpus re-verify) produce BYTE-IDENTICAL canonical result bundles (wall-clock excluded from canonical payloads by construction). FALSIFIER: any byte difference between the three clean bundles, or any clean-run verdict that is not ALLOW/PASS on every gate.
prediction.P5_check1_bit_identical_resume: CHECK 1: the fresh-process full replay AND the checkpoint(317)-resume continuation are BOTH byte-identical to the uninterrupted run (the frozen-ref pattern: sha-pinned trajectory bytes, raw-byte files, no shell redirection). FALSIFIER: one byte differs in either comparison.
prediction.P6_check2_derived_margin_holds: CHECK 2 on the three registered open-loop cases (identical pinned command streams into builds N and N+1): max|v_N1 - v_N| <= delta*V/(1.01*0.95) = 0.03103119967715015 m/s on EVERY case, where V = a_max/(damping*0.95) = 2.977443609022557 m/s is the drive fixed-point envelope (a_max = STRIDE_GAIN*stride_amp_hi = 0.99, d_lo = 0.35*0.95 = 0.3325; the pre-data amendment corrected the baseline to the declared warm-start damping floor), and the closed-loop runs on both builds satisfy |v_t| <= V = 2.977443609022557 m/s at every tick. The measured deltas are recorded per case as evidence. FALSIFIER: any open-loop case exceeding the derived bound, or any closed-loop tick escaping the envelope.
prediction.P7_check3_requal_and_refusal: CHECK 3: the closed-loop requalification runner on build N+1 recomputes every observation and action FROM THE NEW TRAJECTORY (the runner's only input channels are the policy bundle, the scene build, and the entry state), passes all hard gates (bounds honored per the manifest limiter, no NaN/Inf, intervention_reason 'none' at every tick, contact_count >= 2, availability groups exactly as the scope declares, |v_t| <= V = 2.977443609022557 m/s at every tick), and REFUSES any action-replay input with the named error ACTION_REPLAY_REFUSED -- the refusal is itself exercised in the tests. The certificate issued from the clean run validates; a deployment request with any mismatched tuple component BLOCKS. FALSIFIER: any hard gate red on the clean run, the runner accepting an action-replay input, an issued certificate failing its own validator, or a mismatched-tuple deployment request being allowed.

falsifier.F1_silent_promotion: an injected incompatible change (perturbed state hash, swapped normalization constant, altered action mapping) DEPLOYS UNDETECTED -> the gate FAILS; DETECTION (validate violation, deploy BLOCK, or corpus byte movement) = the gate PASSES. Both F1 injections plus the F3 mapping injection are run for real; a single undetected injection fires.
falsifier.F2_resume_drift: a checkpoint restart that would change the future trajectory (dropped cache / dropped RNG in the restart state) NOT detected -- structurally or dynamically -- or a bit-identical resume claimed for anything but the complete snapshot. Only a bit-identical resume may stay silent.
falsifier.F3_legacy_action_drift: any action-bit difference on the frozen observation/command corpus in the same runtime that goes UNDETECTED. The corpus and its harness are built NOW against the dummy actor through P3's frozen loader; the corpus bytes and the runtime are pinned in the certificate.
falsifier.FP_no_false_positives: the three clean runs differing in any byte, or any clean gate red -- the gate crying wolf on unchanged artifacts is the symmetric failure and fires this falsifier.
